CLINICAL FEATURES OF OBESITY
Assessment.
- Body mass index (BMI) is a surrogate measure for global adiposity for ease
of clinical use.
- Waist circumference: is a surrogate marker for truncal obesity.

BMI is calculated as follows
- BMI = weight in kg divided by the square of the height in metres expressed
as kg/m2
Classification of Obesity
- Underweight: <18.5 kg/m2
- Normal weight: 18.5 - 24.9 kg/m2
- Overweight: 25 - 29.9 kg/m2
- Obesity (Class1): 30 - 34.9 kg/m2
- Obesity (Class 2): 35 - 39.9 kg/m2
- Morbid obesity (Class 3): > 40 kg/m2
- Super morbid obesity: > 50 kg/m2
Truncal obesity: waist circumference (WC) and/or waist/hip ratio (WHR).
- A healthy waist circumference for males is <94 cm and< 80cm for females.
- WC of >102 cm in males and >88 cm in females are associated with greatly
increased risks.
- A healthy WHR is <0.9 in males and <0.85 in females.
